Seminar Title:

Piperlongumine Targets BIRC5 to Suppress Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Integrated Computational and Experimental Study

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Life Science

Speaker Name:

Sachidananda Behera

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

LS Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

05 Nov 2026 04:00 PM

Contact:

9348214792

Abstract:

Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is still a major clinical problem and needs an effective and selective therapeutic agent. Piperlongumine (PIP), a bioactive alkaloid of Piper longum, has been shown to have anticancer activity in OSCC, although molecular targets and mechanisms are still not known completely. In this study, an integrated bioinformatics, computational and experimental approaches were used to investigate the anti-cancer potential of PIP. Common OSCC-associated DEGs were detected from three OSCC gene expression datasets, and protein-protein interaction and functional enrichment analyses were subsequently performed. The PIP-related targets were prioritized using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, MM/PBSA, free-energy landscape, and ADMET analyses. The findings were then confirmed with 2D and 3D culture of SCC9 and H357 tumor cells. Among the 444 OSCC-associated DEGs, BIRC5, CDK1, BUB1, BIRC5, and KIF23 were determined as hub genes of which all except MAD2L1 were linked to poor patient survival. MD simulation and MM/PBSA showed that BIRC5 has a stable free-energy landscape and favourable binding energy (-102.938 ± 5.488 kJ/mol). PIP selectively suppressed OSCC growth, enhanced ROS production, reduced MMP led to DNA damage, G2/M arrest and apoptosis, and down-regulated the expression of hub-gene, suggesting BIRC5 as a potential molecular target.
